- .claude/settings.json:25-28, workflow-templates/.claude/settings.json:25-28 | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The broad `claude/*` push allow globs can match refspecs targeting branches outside the intended `claude/*` namespace, including sensitive destinations and deletion refspecs, without prompting.
  WHY: The highest severity was BLOCKER (Gemini); the other reviewers rated this MAJOR, because the ask rules do not cover all such refspecs and the allow globs can bypass confirmation.
- .claude/settings.json:28, workflow-templates/.claude/settings.json:28 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The lease glob and destination glob are independent, allowing a force-with-lease push to check one `claude/*` branch while overwriting another.
  WHY: The lease check does not protect the destination branch's current state, and the merged-PR guard does not prevent this mismatch for non-merged branches.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/write-plan.md:17 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The push retry instructions do not say to retry as a new plain command, contradicting §21.E's prohibition on push retry loops.
  WHY: Pushes inside shell control flow can cause the merged-PR guard to ask for confirmation in every permission mode.
- .claude/settings.json:27-28, .claude/settings.json:73-86 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The permission rules rely on ask rules taking precedence over allow rules, but that precedence is not tested.
  WHY: If allow rules are evaluated first, a push such as `claude/x:main` could proceed without the intended confirmation.

- requirement: Verify the new interactive push allow and ask rules with tests; the PR description says the push forms were tested and the listed tests all pass.
  expected_change_site: `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py` or a dedicated test for `.claude/settings.json` permissions
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: The PR diff adds no test cases for the new interactive `permissions.allow` or `permissions.ask` rules; the cited existing tests do not assert those rules, and only live/template parity is checked.
- requirement: The PR says sessions should use one plain push command and never a retry loop, but the shipped commands still instruct push retries with backoff.
  expected_change_site: `.claude/commands/write-plan.md:17`, `.claude/commands/audit-plans.md:53`, `.claude/commands/apply-analysis.md:13`, `.claude/commands/implement-plan-ai.md:13`, `.claude/commands/verify-activation.md:83`, `.claude/commands/seed-repo.md:20` and their `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/` twins
  confidence=[4]

  EVIDENCE: The PR diff does not touch these command files; the cited instructions still tell sessions to retry pushes with backoff, including within the merged-PR guard's shell matcher.

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .claude/settings.json (and the identical workflow-templates/.claude/settings.json) | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The trailing `*` in the permission glob matches any text after `claude/`, spaces included. The new `ask` rules catch only `main` and `master` as destinations, plus `--delete`, `-d` and `--prune`. A force-with-lease push that names an extra destination or refspec passes with no prompt. Examples are `git push --force-with-lease origin claude/x:release` and `git push --force-with-lease origin claude/x release-branch`. A space-separated deletion refspec such as `claude/x :release` is also allowed. The merged-PR guard only checks branches that belong to merged PRs, so it does not stop these.
  WHY: A session can force-overwrite or delete a non-`claude/*` remote branch other than `main` or `master` without any approval. The CLAUDE.md §21.E text and the changelog say a `claude/*` allow rule "never silently carries a default-branch write or a deletion". That holds only for `main`/`master`, and this change adds a force variant to the allow list. Deletion through a colon refspec is not covered, and neither are other protected branch names.
- .claude/settings.json | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The lease glob and the destination glob are independent. A command can set the lease on `claude/a` and push to `claude/b`.
  WHY: The lease check protects a different branch from the one being overwritten. Both branches are inside the `claude/` namespace, so the damage is limited to another session's working branch. That is a weaker guarantee than the §21.E text implies.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/write-plan.md:17 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The same retry wording is in audit-plans.md:53, apply-analysis.md:13 and implement-plan-ai.md:13. It contradicts the new §21.E rule against push retry loops, and nothing in the PR tells these commands to retry as a new call. These files are outside the PR's changed files.
  WHY: A session following those commands can write the retry loop that makes the merged-PR guard ask for confirmation in every permission mode. That is the problem this PR set out to remove. I am raising it as a documentation inconsistency rather than a defect in this diff.
- .claude/settings.json | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The change widens the effective capability of interactive sessions (force pushes are now auto-allowed). It relies on ask rules taking precedence over allow rules when both match. That precedence is not tested anywhere in the repo.
  WHY: If a Claude Code release evaluated the allow rule first, a push of `claude/x:main` would go through without a prompt. The PR description says this was checked only by running the merged-PR guard, not the permission matcher itself.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: Add two allow rules and twelve `ask` rules, with the PR description claiming "tests … all pass".
  Expected change site: A contract test, for example in `tests/test_claude_template_live_parity.py` or a new settings-policy test, that asserts the allow and ask rules in `.claude/settings.json`. The existing `tests/test_claude_settings_policy.py` covers only the unattended engine template.
  Evidence of absence: The diff adds no test file. A repo search for `git push -u origin claude` finds no test that pins the interactive `permissions.allow` or `permissions.ask` lists. Only the byte parity between the live file and its template is checked. A later edit could drop or loosen an ask rule without any test failing.
  SEVERITY: high
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .claude/settings.json, Lines 27-28 | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The allow rules Bash(git push --force-with-lease origin claude/*) and Bash(git push --force-with-lease=claude/* origin claude/*) are overly broad because they use globs that can match refspecs targeting sensitive branches.
  WHY: These globs match commands such as git push --force-with-lease origin claude/feature-a:main. Since allow rules are matched before ask rules, these commands bypass the confirmation prompt intended for destructive pushes to default branches.
- .claude/settings.json, Lines 27-28 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The rule Bash(git push --force-with-lease=claude/* origin claude/*) permits independent globs for the lease target branch and the push destination branch.
  WHY: A push could be executed that checks the lease status for one branch (e.g., claude/feature-a) but pushes to and potentially overwrites a different branch (e.g., claude/feature-b), as the merged-PR guard does not block this behavior for non-merged branches.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/write-plan.md, Line 17 (and corresponding locations in audit-plans.md, apply-analysis.md, and implement-plan-ai.md) | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The command instructions advise retrying pushes with exponential backoff but fail to specify that each retry must be a new, plain command call.
  WHY: Pushes wrapped in shell control flow (for loops) prevent the merged-PR guard from resolving the directory of the push, causing confirmation prompts in all permission modes, violating the intent of minimizing prompts.
- .claude/settings.json, Lines 27-28 | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The allow rules use broad globs (*) that permit destructive pushes (e.g., --delete, --prune) or pushes to sensitive targets (main, master) if they happen to contain the string claude/.
  WHY: The allow rules match any command string containing the glob, and since they appear before the ask rules, they circumvent the confirmation mechanism for these dangerous operations.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Ran `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` on these push forms. The plain `--force-with-lease` forms are allowed without a prompt... [and] all pass."
  Expected change site: tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py (or a new dedicated test file)
  Evidence of absence: PR DIFF does not add any new test cases. Existing tests in tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py do not assert anything about the new permissions.allow or permissions.ask rules in .claude/settings.json, failing to verify that the new forms behave as intended or that dangerous forms are caught by the ask rules.
  SEVERITY: high
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/settings.json, workflow-templates/.claude/settings.json, line 28 — `"Bash(git push --force-with-lease=claude/* origin claude/*)"`
  PROBLEM: The allow rule uses two independent `claude/*` globs with no anchoring between them. Claude Code's permission matcher matches the lease ref argument and the destination ref argument separately, so a push like `git push --force-with-lease=claude/feature-a:<sha> origin claude/feature-b` satisfies both globs even when the lease target (`claude/feature-a`) and the destination (`claude/feature-b`) are different branches. Git's `--force-with-lease=<ref>:<sha>` form only verifies `<ref>`'s remote SHA before allowing the force-push, so the destination branch can be silently overwritten without checking its current state.
  WHY: A session can push the local `claude/feature-a` refspec against the `claude/feature-b` remote, satisfying this allow rule (and the merged-PR guard's check on `claude/feature-a`), while the `claude/feature-b` remote branch's prior history is replaced by `claude/feature-a`'s commits. The pre-existing rule `Bash(git push origin claude/*)` (line 26) was tightened later (the merge-train / QA process); this new rule re-introduces the independent-glob pattern that the surrounding rules never had.
- .claude/settings.json, workflow-templates/.claude/settings.json, lines 25-28 (the four `Bash(git push … claude/*)` allow rules)
  PROBLEM: The trailing `*` in `claude/*` matches more text than the branch name.
